Differences and ratios between strata, path by path

Source: R/derive-observed.R
mt_contrast.Rd

Compares a derived quantity (life expectancy, age-standardised rate, probability of dying, death rate of one age group, or an index of lifespan variation) between the levels of a stratum variable and a reference level, path by path, so that the interval of the difference includes the joint uncertainty of both strata. Strata are matched on all other stratum variables (for example the deprivation gap within each sex).

Usage

mt_contrast(
  x,
  var,
  ref,
  quantity = c("life_expectancy", "asr", "prob_dying", "rate", "lifespan_variation"),
  type = c("difference", "ratio"),
  probs = c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975),
  ...
)

Arguments

x

An mt_draws object (forecast) or an mt_data object (observed, see mt_observed()).

var

Stratum variable to compare across (for example "quintile").

ref

Reference level of var.

quantity

"life_expectancy", "asr", "prob_dying", "rate" or "lifespan_variation".

type

"difference" (level minus reference) or "ratio".

probs

Quantile levels.

...

Arguments of the quantity: at for life expectancy, standard, per, exposure and age_groups for asr(), from and to for prob_dying(), age (an age label) for "rate", measure (one index, default "edagger") and at for lifespan_variation().

Value

A data.table with the other stratum variables, level, ref, period, mean, quantiles and p_positive, the share of paths with a positive difference (or a ratio above 1). For forecasts this is the predictive probability of a positive difference under the model. For observed data it is the share of the Poisson bootstrap draws (see mt_observed()) with a positive difference, which is neither a p-value nor a posterior probability.

Examples

x <- mt_example(deaths = "single", years = 2001:2015)
fc <- mt_forecast(mt_fit(lee_carter(), x), h = 5, n_draws = 100, seed = 1)
mt_contrast(fc, var = "sex", ref = "female", at = 30)
#>     level    ref period      mean    q0.025      q0.5    q0.975 p_positive
#>    <char> <char>  <num>     <num>     <num>     <num>     <num>      <num>
#> 1:   male female   2016 -5.045323 -5.267886 -5.043577 -4.815912          0
#> 2:   male female   2017 -5.066032 -5.465374 -5.047023 -4.744987          0
#> 3:   male female   2018 -5.048624 -5.553453 -5.048755 -4.584807          0
#> 4:   male female   2019 -5.046785 -5.582633 -5.084452 -4.584923          0
#> 5:   male female   2020 -5.053376 -5.656648 -5.065486 -4.416842          0
#>           quantity       type
#>             <char>     <char>
#> 1: life_expectancy difference
#> 2: life_expectancy difference
#> 3: life_expectancy difference
#> 4: life_expectancy difference
#> 5: life_expectancy difference
